name: Pinochle Double Deck
description: Partnership trick-and-meld game for four players using two 40-card pinochle packs (80 cards, nines removed). Bid to name trump, meld for points, then play 20 tricks; first team to reach the target score (e.g. 1500) wins.

overview.description: Partnership trick-and-meld game for four players using two 40-card pinochle packs (80 cards, nines removed). Bid to name trump, meld for points, then play 20 tricks; first team to reach the target score (e.g. 1500) wins.

history.origins: Pinochle descends from the European games bezique and Binokel. German immigrants brought Binokel to America in the last quarter of the 19th century, where it was mispronounced and spelled as pinochle; it became popular among American Jewish and Irish immigrant communities. The double-deck variant uses two 40-card pinochle packs (80 cards total, nines removed) for four-player partnership play, with hand sizes and minimum bids scaled up; it shares this American cultural origin and was likewise temporarily banned in some US cities during World War I due to anti-German sentiment, before regaining popularity.
timeline: Late 19th century: German immigrants brought Binokel to America; game adopted as Pinochle. Double-deck variant used for four-player partnership play.

setup.players: Four players in two partnerships; partners sit opposite.
setup.dealing: All 80 cards dealt, 20 per player; typically in packets of four or five, clockwise from left of dealer.

rules.objective: Partnerships bid for the right to name trump; the bidding team must meet their contract by combining meld points and trick points. First partnership to reach the agreed target score (e.g. 1500) wins.
rules.gameplay: Each hand has three phases: auction (players bid; high bidder declares trump), melding (all players show melds; points counted), and trick play (high bidder leads; follow suit; trump wins if unable to follow). Trick points plus meld must meet or exceed the bid or the team is set (bid subtracted).

scoring.description: Meld points plus trick points (counters) per hand; bidding team must make contract or is set (bid subtracted). First partnership to reach target (e.g. 1500) wins.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach the agreed target score (commonly 1000 or 1500) wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: Pinochle with double deck (80 cards); four players.
